name: Rasteau

limits: For red wine, Grenache: at least 50%
For red wine, Mourvèdre and Syrah together: at least 20%
rules.yield_base: 38 hl/ha for red, 30 hl/ha of must for fortified

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.

notes: Southern Rhône reds blend Grenache, Syrah, Mourvèdre, Carignan and Cinsault, a mix known elsewhere as GSM.
Syrah adds structure and color to Grenache in blends such as Côtes du Rhône and Châteauneuf-du-Pape.
Reds from the left bank are full bodied and tannic when young, with aromas of prune, undergrowth, chocolate and ripe black fruit.
Right bank reds are slightly lighter and fruitier.

blurb.text: A southern Rhône appellation covering fortified and unfortified wines, led by Grenache. Sweet fortified wines can be red, rosé or white. Dry red wines were added.
